title: Focus and composition events
learningObjectives: Explain focus and composition events and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Focus events include focus, blur, focusin, and focusout. Composition events describe text input composition, especially for input methods used by languages that assemble characters through intermediate composition. Input handlers should avoid prematurely treating incomplete composition text as final input.
understand.whyItMatters: Multilingual text entry must work with IMEs. Search and validation code that reacts to every input event without checking composition state can disrupt users typing Telugu, Japanese, Chinese, and other scripts.
understand.analogy: Composition is like drafting a character through several steps before confirming the final text; the interface should not interrupt the draft.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The example avoids triggering its search action while the user is composing text through an IME and processes the completed value afterward.

examples.explanation: The example avoids triggering its search action while the user is composing text through an IME and processes the completed value afterward.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Test a search field with an IME. Use compositionstart and compositionend to prevent premature filtering while a character sequence is being composed.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which events mark the beginning and end of IME text composition?
questions.explanation: These events identify the composition session around IME text entry.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
